summary.headline: Tilaknagar Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 166% YoY to Rs 1,046 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.1% amid packaging inflation.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with Imperial Blue (IB) inside the combined business, with volumes up 172% YoY and 9% QoQ, led by IB at 5.4 million cases (+18% QoQ). NSR rose to Rs 1,183 per case (+1.5% QoQ, +5.3% YoY), but glass-led packaging inflation compressed gross margin to 42.1% (adjusted for subsidy) from 45.2% in Q4 FY26. Adjusted-for-subsidy EBITDA was Rs 148 crore at 14.5%, and net debt rose to Rs 2,100 crore on working-capital build. Management reiterated FY27 volume guidance and a net debt target of about Rs 1,700 crore by March 2027.

segments.name: Imperial Blue (IB)
segments.commentary: Volume 5.4 million cases in Q1, up 18% QoQ; June 2026 was the highest ever monthly volume at 3.4 million cases company-wide, with IB the largest-selling deluxe whisky. Reintroduced in Delhi in July 2026.

segments.name: MHB
segments.commentary: Volume grew 7% YoY in Q1 despite April disruptions.

segments.name: Super premium and luxury (House of TI / SSL)
segments.commentary: Spaceman Spirits (SSL) more than doubled sales YoY in Q1; growth led by Samsara Pink and new Indian-flavour launches. House:Pour Picante ready-to-pour launched late in Q1. Monarch Legacy Edition Brandy and Seven Islands Pure Malt are being expanded.

segments.name: Bartisans (associate)
segments.commentary: Stake increased from 36.2% to 41.5% to fund quick-commerce expansion and product innovation.

guidance_outlook: FY27: high single-digit to low double-digit volume growth for the combined business maintained; IB full-year volume expected to grow double digits from the ~21.5 million cases base at acquisition.
Beyond FY27: annual volume growth in mid-teens over the next couple of years; revenue growth at least ~300 bps above volume growth; new launches from FY28 onwards.

EBITDA margin for combined business 16%-18% by FY29 with upward bias; FY27 margin to improve from 15.5% base set in Q4 FY26. Q3 and Q4 expected to show significant margin uptick; Q2 similar to Q1 with extra A&SP spend.
Net debt target about Rs 1,700 crore by March 2027 (reduction of ~Rs 400 crore); net debt/EBITDA below 1.0x by March 2029 (earlier FY29 framing).
Supply chain and packaging optimisation expected to expand acquired-business margins by 250-400 bps and consolidated margins by ~250 bps.
Telangana price increase expected soon; management estimates 150-200 bps incremental annualised margin impact.
capex_capacity: IB manufacturing integration about 90% complete by April 2026; one state (of the TSMA-linked states) still under TSMA, with transition targeted by March 2027.
IB now transitioned from TSMA into Tilaknagar-operated units for 90% of the business.
Prag Distillery: around 60%-70% of the expected bottling-related savings already reflected in the numbers; full benefit not yet visible. Utilisation rate not disclosed.
Sales team scaled from about 350 pre-acquisition to 850+ as of March 31, 2026, across North, West, Central and East India.
demand_pricing: Glass and other packaging inputs inflated due to geopolitical tensions; partly offset by softer ENA prices.
Karnataka: volumes and operating-segment market share improved after price reduction and slab reduction.
Market share of IB improved in all states versus exit levels; South the easiest transition, and share gains in North, East and West (Maharashtra) as well.

Competition intensifying in IB's price segment (ICONiQ White, McDowell's scotch); management expects category activation to help growth. A&SP reinvestment rate being raised; activations in 28,000+ outlets in Q1.
Delhi: IB peak was about 0.5 million cases (around 2019-20); management expects return to those levels in 12-18 months.
Maharashtra-made liquor category around 6-7 lakh cases per month, flat; IB gaining share in the state.
Tamil Nadu business under 0.5 million cases annualised; possible policy change under new state government (imports or market opening) seen as upside.

qa_highlights.question: Karnataka post-reform competition and pricing for IB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reported good volume uptake and significantly improved operating-segment market share since the price reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Which states show more or less IB traction versus average?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined state-level detail; said share improved in every state versus exit levels, with South the smoothest transition.

qa_highlights.question: Are IB-related disruptions in Odisha, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Karnataka TSMA-related?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the disruptions were predominantly IB-specific and TSMA-related; details were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Trade spend and growth in the low-prestige IB segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said segment activity is rising after years of inactivity by leaders; company is increasing A&SP reinvestment and activating in 28,000+ outlets.

qa_highlights.question: Margin recovery timing to 15.5% and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumes inflation status quo; Q3 and Q4 to see significant margin uptick, Q2 similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Quarterly IB run-rate and separate IB NSR?
qa_highlights.answer: No bifurcated NSR given; IB full-year double-digit volume growth expected.

qa_highlights.question: Telangana price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry in talks with government; last increase was three years ago; expected to add 150-200 bps to margin annualised.

qa_highlights.question: Tamil Nadu market size and route-to-market risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Current TN business under 0.5 million cases annualised; upside if imports or market opening allowed under new government.
